# 2025 AFP Payments Fraud and Control Survey Report — Key Highlights

- **URL:** https://www.truist.com/content/dam/truist-bank/us/en/documents/info/cci/2025-afp-payments-fraud-control-survey-report-key-highlights.pdf
- **Publisher:** Association for Financial Professionals (AFP), underwritten by Truist
- **Retrieved:** 2026-08-10
- **Topic:** vendor-master-bec-fraud

## Summary

The 21st annual AFP Payments Fraud and Control Survey, fielded **January 2025** with **521 responses** from corporate practitioners; all results reflect **calendar-year 2024** data. Published **April 2025**. This highlights edition carries the headline percentages; the full report is AFP-member only.

### Overall fraud prevalence

- **79%** of organizations experienced actual or attempted payments fraud in 2024, down from **80%** in 2023. The 2022 reading was an outlier low of **65%**.
- Full series (percent of organizations, 2009→2024): 73, 71, 68, 61, 60, 62, 73, 74, 78, 82, 81, 74, 71, 65, 80, 79.
- By size: annual revenue **< $1B = 73%**; **≥ $1B = 83%**; **≥ $1B with fewer than 26 payment accounts = 84%**; **≥ $1B with more than 100 payment accounts = 79%**.

### Payment methods subject to attempted/actual fraud (2024, with 2023 comparison)

| Method | 2024 | 2023 |
|---|---|---|
| Checks | 63% | 65% |
| ACH debits | 38% | 33% |
| Wire transfers | 30% | 24% |
| Corporate/commercial credit cards | 21% | 20% |
| ACH credits | 20% | 19% |
| Cash | 5% | 4% |
| Virtual cards | 5% | 3% |
| Mobile wallets | 3% | 1% |
| Faster payments (RTP, FedNow) | 2% | 1% |
| Cryptocurrency | 1% | — |

Checks were hit at **70%** for organizations ≥ $1B revenue versus **55%** for those < $1B.

### Origination of fraud attempts (2024) — the vendor-master-relevant taxonomy

BEC **62%**; individual external to the organization using non-email tactics (forged check, stolen card, corporate synthetic identity) **49%**; **vendor imposter 45%**; **invoice fraud 24%**; U.S. Postal Service office interference **23%**; imposter to a client posing as a representative of your company **14%**; third-party/outsourcer **12%**; account takeover **12%**; compromised mobile device **8%**; organized crime ring **7%**; deep-fake attempt **5%**; ransomware **4%**; internal party (malicious insider) **3%**.

Vendor imposter fraud rose sharply from **34%** (2023) to **45%** (2024); invoice fraud rose from **14%** to **24%**.

### BEC specifics

- **63%** of organizations experienced BEC in 2024, unchanged from 2023 (2014→2024 series: 71, 64, 74, 77, 80, 75, 76, 68, 71, 63, 63).
- BEC by size: < $1B **62%**; ≥ $1B **64%**; ≥ $1B & <26 payment accounts **59%**; ≥ $1B & >100 payment accounts **69%**.
- Payment methods used in BEC: wire transfers **63%** (up from 39%), ACH credits **50%** (up from 47%), checks **26%**, ACH debits **26%** (up from 18% and 20% respectively), corporate cards **11%**, third-party payouts **9%**, cash **8%**, gift cards **6%**, mobile wallets **4%**, cryptocurrency **3%**, RTP/FedNow **3%**.
- **Spoof emails** remain the most prevalent BEC type, cited by **79%** (up from 77% in 2023).
- "Classic" BEC (impersonating a senior executive to request a transfer) **declined to 49%** in 2024 from **57%** in 2023; **vendor impersonation rose to 60%**; **third-party impersonation was the most frequent BEC type at 63%**.
- BEC prevention policies: **66%** fully implemented, **17%** documented, **10%** reviewed, **7%** testing. Fully-implemented rates by segment: < $1B **59%**, ≥ $1B **72%**, ≥ $1B & <26 accounts **68%**, ≥ $1B & >100 accounts **79%**.

### Detection and recovery

- **35%** of victims took **less than one week** to uncover the fraud; **21%** detected it **within one to two weeks**.
- **Treasury** is the department most likely to uncover both attempted and actual payments fraud, followed by **accounts payable**. More than half of practitioners report **AP is the department most vulnerable to email fraud**.
- Recovery distribution of lost funds (2024): **more than 75% recovered = 22%**; 51–75% = **12%**; 26–50% = **18%**; 11–25% = **12%**; less than 10% = **17%**; **not recovered at all = 20%**. In 2023, **41%** recouped more than 75% and **30%** recovered nothing; **58%** recouped up to 75% in 2024 vs **29%** in 2023.

### Check exposure

**91%** of respondents currently use checks (up from 75% in 2023); **75%** have no plan to eliminate checks in the next two years. Annual check usage: 10% or less of payments = **41%**, 11–25% = **29%**, 26–50% = **20%**, over 50% = **10%**. **23%** experienced check fraud due to mailbox theft.

## Eval-relevant hooks

- Decision rule: **vendor imposter (45%) plus invoice fraud (24%)** together now rival classic executive-impersonation BEC — a control-design task should weight vendor-master and invoice controls at least as heavily as CEO-fraud training.
- Checkable assertions: 79% payments-fraud prevalence in 2024; BEC 63%; wire transfers the top BEC-targeted method at 63%; vendor imposter 45% (up from 34%).
- Scoring hook for a "who owns detection" task: **Treasury** detects most fraud, **AP** is the most vulnerable department — an org-design answer that puts sole detection responsibility in AP is wrong per this source.
- Recovery-expectation hook: only **22%** recover more than 75% of losses and **20%** recover nothing — usable to grade whether an agent treats recall as reliable (it is not).
- Maturity-model hook: BEC policy states form a 4-level ladder — **documented (17%) → reviewed (10%) → tested (7%) → fully implemented (66%)** — a checkable taxonomy for a controls-maturity assessment task.
- Size-risk rule: fraud prevalence rises with revenue (83% at ≥$1B vs 73% at <$1B) and BEC rises with payment-account sprawl (69% at >100 accounts vs 59% at <26).
